arxiv-2012-05415.title: Diffusion of active particles with angular velocity reversal
arxiv-2012-05415.creator: Kristian Stølevik Olsen
arxiv-2012-05415.description: Abstract Biological and synthetic microswimmers display a wide range of swimming trajectories depending on driving forces and torques. In this paper we consider a simple overdamped model of self-propelled particles with a constant self-propulsion speed, but an angular velocity that varies in time.

arxiv-2204-04741.title: Is GitHub’s Copilot as Bad as Humans at Introducing Vulnerabilities in Code?
arxiv-2204-04741.creator: Owura Asare*, Meiyappan Nagappan, N. Asokan
arxiv-2204-04741.description: Abstract Several advances in deep learning have been successfully applied to the software development process. Of recent interest is the use of neural language models to build tools, such as Copilot, that assist in writing code. In this paper we perform a comparative empirical analysis of Copilot-generated code from a security perspective.

arxiv-2207-09378.title: P4TE: PISA Switch Based Traffic Engineering in Fat-Tree Data Center Networks (Preprint: Accepted for publication in Elsevier Computer Networks)
arxiv-2207-09378.creator: Debobroto Das Robin, Javed I. Khan
arxiv-2207-09378.description: Abstract This work presents P4TE, an in-band traffic monitoring, load-aware packet forwarding, and flow rate controlling mechanism for traffic engineering in fat-tree topology-based data center networks using PISA switches. It achieves sub-RTT reaction time to change in network conditions, improved flow completion time, and balanced link utilization.

arxiv-2212-11672.title: Trustworthy Social Bias Measurement
arxiv-2212-11672.creator: Rishi Bommasani, Percy Liang
arxiv-2212-11672.description: Abstract How do we design measures of social bias that we trust ? While prior work has introduced several measures, no measure has gained widespread trust: instead, mounting evidence argues we should distrust these measures. In this work, we design bias measures that warrant trust based on the cross-disciplinary theory of measurement modeling.

arxiv-2302-02357.title: Ice melting in salty water: layering and non-monotonic dependence on the mean salinity
arxiv-2302-02357.creator: Rui Yang, Christopher J. Howland, Hao-Ran Liu, Roberto Verzicco, Detlef Lohse
arxiv-2302-02357.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Rui Yang, Christopher J. Howland, Hao-Ran Liu, Roberto Verzicco, Detlef Lohse. The presence of salt in ocean water strongly affects the melt rate and the shape evolution of ice, both of utmost relevance in geophysical and ocean flow and thus for the climate. To get a better quantitative understanding of the physical mechanics at play in ice melting in salty water, we numerically investigate the lateral melting of an ice block in stably stratified saline water, using a realistic, nonlinear equation of state (EOS).

arxiv-2304-10161.title: Erratum and addendum to the paper: Abundance for Kähler threefolds
arxiv-2304-10161.creator: Frédéric Campana, Andreas Höring, Thomas Peternell
arxiv-2304-10161.description: Abstract . In this text we signal a serious gap in the proof of the main theorem of our paper and explain which parts of the statement remain valid. In fact, the main theorem remains valid unless possibly the variety does not admit positive-dimensional subvarieties through a very general point and is not bimeromorphic to a quotient of a torus.

arxiv-2307-08596.title: Omnipotent Adversarial Training in the Wild
arxiv-2307-08596.creator: Guanlin Li, Kangjie Chen, Yuan Xu, Han Qiu, Tianwei Zhang
arxiv-2307-08596.description: Abstract Adversarial training is an important topic in robust deep learning, but the community lacks attention to its practical usage. In this paper, we aim to resolve a real-world challenge, i.e., training a model on an imbalanced and noisy dataset to achieve high clean accuracy and adversarial robustness, with our proposed Omnipotent Adversarial Training ( OAT ) strategy.

arxiv-2307-13255.title: A note on ”The Klein-Gordon oscillator in (1+2)-dimensions Gürses space-time backgrounds (Ann. Phys. (N. Y.) 404 (2019) 1)”
arxiv-2307-13255.creator: Omar Mustafa, Faizuddin Ahmed
arxiv-2307-13255.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Omar Mustafa, Faizuddin Ahmed. Abstract: We revisit and discuss the KG-oscillator in the ( 1 + 2 ) (1+2) -dimensional Gürses space-time studied in Ref. The modified oscillator frequency i.e., ω ~ 2 = ( Ω 2 ​ E 2 + η 2 ) \tilde{\omega}^{2}=(\Omega^{2}\,E^{2}+\eta^{2}) appeared in the eigenvalue equation is an energy-dependent parameter, and consequently, the results are accurately reported here. Moreover, we show some interesting spectroscopic features indulged within the very nature of Gürses space-time for the KG-Gürses oscillators.

arxiv-2309-07696.title: Steady-state entanglement production in a quantum thermal machine with continuous feedback control
arxiv-2309-07696.creator: Giovanni Francesco Diotallevi, Björn Annby-Andersson, Peter Samuelsson, Armin Tavakoli, Pharnam Bakhshinezhad
arxiv-2309-07696.description: Abstract Quantum thermal machines can generate steady-state entanglement by harvesting spontaneous interactions with local environments. However, using minimal resources and control, the entanglement is typically very noisy. Here, we study entanglement generation in a two-qubit quantum thermal machine in the presence of a continuous feedback protocol.

arxiv-2407-14103.title: Zero-Shot Underwater Gesture Recognition
arxiv-2407-14103.creator: Sandipan Sarma, Gundameedi Sai Ram Mohan, Hariansh Sehgal, Arijit Sur
arxiv-2407-14103.description: Abstract Hand gesture recognition allows humans to interact with machines non-verbally, which has a huge application in underwater exploration using autonomous underwater vehicles. Recently, a new gesture-based language called CADDIAN has been devised for divers, and supervised learning methods have been applied to recognize the gestures with high accuracy.

arxiv-2411-07429.title: The extended Hubbard model on a honeycomb lattice
arxiv-2411-07429.creator: Welberth Kennedy, Sebastião dos Anjos Sousa-Júnior, Natanael C. Costa, Raimundo R. dos Santos
arxiv-2411-07429.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Welberth Kennedy, Sebastião dos Anjos Sousa-Júnior, Natanael C. Costa, Raimundo R. dos Santos. The lack of both nesting and a van Hove singularity at half filling, together with the presence of Dirac cones makes the honeycomb lattice a special laboratory to explore strongly correlated phenomena.

arxiv-2503-05416.title: Subgroups of symmetric groups: enumeration and asymptotic properties
arxiv-2503-05416.creator: Colva M. Roney-Dougal and Gareth Tracey
arxiv-2503-05416.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Colva M. Roney-Dougal and Gareth Tracey. In this paper, we prove that the symmetric group S n {\mathrm{S}}_{n} has 2 n 2 / 16 + o ⁡ ( n 2 ) 2^{n^{2}/16+o(n^{2})} subgroups, settling a conjecture of Pyber from 1993. We also derive asymptotically sharp upper and lower bounds on the number of subgroups of S n {\mathrm{S}}_{n} of various kinds, including the number of p p -subgroups. In addition, we prove a range of theorems about random subgroups of S n {\mathrm{S}}_{n} .

arxiv-2506-21499.title: Lightweight Physics-Informed Zero-Shot Ultrasound Plane Wave Denoising
arxiv-2506-21499.creator: Hojat Asgariandehkordi*, Mostafa Sharifzadeh*, Hassan Rivaz
arxiv-2506-21499.description: Abstract Ultrasound Coherent Plane Wave Compounding (CPWC) enhances image contrast by combining echoes from multiple steered transmissions. While increasing the number of angles generally improves image quality, it drastically reduces the frame rate and can introduce blurring artifacts in fast-moving targets. Moreover, compounded images remain susceptible to noise, particularly when acquired with a limited number of transmissions.

europmc-pmc7255168.description: Background Although mortality due to COVID-19 is, for the most part, robustly tracked, its indirect effect at the population level through lockdown, lifestyle changes, and reorganisation of health-care systems has not been evaluated. We aimed to assess the incidence and outcomes

pmc-10674221.title: Sea Cucumber Peptides Ameliorate DSS-Induced Ulcerative Colitis: The Role of the Gut Microbiota, the Intestinal Barrier, and Macrophage Polarization
pmc-10674221.creator: Song Yu, Haixiang Guo, Zhonghao Ji, Yi Zheng, Bingbing Wang, Qingqing Chen, Hongyu Tang, Bao Yuan
pmc-10674221.description: The incidence of ulcerative colitis (UC) is increasing annually. There are few treatments for UC patients, and some drugs have serious side effects. Sea cucumber peptide (SCP) has anti-inflammatory, antioxidant and other biological activities, and various sea cucumber species are in pharmaceutical development. However, relevant studies on the effects of SCP on UC progression are still lacking.

pmc-11430411.title: Optimizing the Sensitivity of a Pelvic Sentinel Node Algorithm Requires a Hybrid Algorithm Combining Indocyanine Green Based Mapping and the Removal of Non-Mapped Nodes at Defined Anatomic Positions
pmc-11430411.creator: Michele Bollino, Barbara Geppert, Petur Reynisson, Celine Lönnerfors, Jan Persson, Xavier Sastre-Garau
pmc-11430411.description: Simple SummaryPresent algorithms for the detection of pelvic sentinel lymph utilizing only tracers may fail to detect metastatic disease as women with nodal metastases overall have an overall lower mapping rate and that nodes at certain anatomic positions of the pelvic lymphatic pathways map less frequently.

pmc-11643587.title: Multifunctional Sensor Array for User Interaction Based on Dielectric Elastomers with Sputtered Metal Electrodes
pmc-11643587.creator: Sebastian Gratz-Kelly, Mario Cerino, Daniel Philippi, Dirk Göttel, Sophie Nalbach, Jonas Hubertus, Günter Schultes, John Heppe, Paul Motzki
pmc-11643587.description: The integration of textile-based sensing and actuation elements has become increasingly important across various fields, driven by the growing demand for smart textiles in healthcare, sports, and wearable electronics. This paper presents the development of a small, smart dielectric elastomer (DE)-based sensing array designed for user control input in applications such as human–machine interaction, virtual object manipulation, and robotics.

pmc-11678408.title: Iridium-Catalyzed Highly Selective 1,4-Reduction of α,β-Unsaturated Carbonyl Compounds
pmc-11678408.creator: Youwei Chen, Jide Li, Jiaxi Xu, Zhanhui Yang
pmc-11678408.description: In this study, an iridium-catalyzed selective 1,4-reduction of α,β-unsaturated carbonyl compounds is realized, with water as a solvent and formic acid as a hydride donor. The new efficient iridium catalyst features a 2-(4,5-dihydroimidazol-2-yl)quinoline ligand. The chemoselectivity and catalyst efficiency are highly dependent on the electronic and steric properties of the substrates.

pmc-11726875.title: Exploring Trimethylaminuria: Genetics and Molecular Mechanisms, Epidemiology, and Emerging Therapeutic Strategies
pmc-11726875.creator: Antonina Sidoti, Rosalia D’Angelo, Andrea Castagnetti, Elisa Viciani, Concetta Scimone, Simona Alibrandi, Giuseppe Giannini
pmc-11726875.description: Simple SummaryTrimethylaminuria is a very rare and little-known metabolic syndrome. It is caused by the accumulation of a foul-smelling molecule, trimethylamine, which is excreted through biological fluids such as sweat, determining the symptoms in affected patients, which consist of odor emissions similar to rotten fish. TMA accumulation is determined by both genetic and environmental factors, especially gut dysbiosis.

pmc-12524061.title: CIN2 in the Era of Risk-Based Management and HPV Vaccination: Epidemiology, Natural History and Guidelines
pmc-12524061.creator: Maria Teresa Bruno, Alessia Pagana, Carla Lo Giudice, Marco Marzio Panella, Giuseppe Mascellino, Antonio Simone Laganà
pmc-12524061.description: Background: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 (CIN2) represents a controversial lesion in cervical cancer prevention. Traditionally included in the aggregate CIN2+ endpoint for reasons of diagnostic stability and statistical power, isolated CIN2 has unique biological characteristics: greater interobserver variability, a high probability of spontaneous regression and a lower risk of progression compared to CIN3.
